rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Quraysh asked the Prophet to turn al-Safa into gold so they could strengthen themselves against their enemy; God offered this with a threat of unmatched punishment if they disbelieved, but the Prophet asked to summon them gradually, and this verse was revealed because they already saw greater signs.
rows.anchor: قالت قريش للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم : ادع الله ان يجعل لنا الصفا ذهبا نتقوى به على عدونا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb transmits a prayer attributed to Ezra describing creation and the opening of the treasury of light and wisdom, from which night and day were made to alternate by God's command.
rows.anchor: قال عزير عليه السلام : اللهم بكلمتك خلقت جميع خلقك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi glosses al-fulk as a ship; Sa'id ibn Jubayr is reported to give the same meaning.
rows.anchor: عن السدى عن أبي مالك : الفلك قال : السفينة .

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra says that every drop of rain descends according to a measure.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الجليل عن شهر بن حوشب ان أبا هريرة قال : ما نزل قطر الا بميزان .

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the water descends from the seventh heaven and each drop lands on a cloud like a camel.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة قال : ينزل الله الماء من السماء السابعة

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah describes resurrection bodies being formed from water sent from beneath the Throne, compared to men's semen, just as plants grow from soil; he recites the verse about reviving the earth.
rows.anchor: ثنا أبو الزعراء عن عبد الله قال فيرسل الله عز وجل ماء من تحت العرش

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet explains resurrection by comparing it to land that is barren, then fertile, then barren, then fertile again.
rows.anchor: فقلت : كيف يحيي الله الموتى ؟ قال : ما اتيت على ارض من ارضك وهي مجدبة ؟

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that just as God revives dead earth with water, He will revive people on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قوله عز وجل : فاحيا به الأرض بعد موتها قال : كما احيا الله الأرض الميتة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains “spread” as “created”; Muqatil ibn Hayyan is reported to hold the same gloss.
rows.anchor: عن السدى قوله عز وجل : وبث فيها من كل دابة قال : بث : خلق .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God can make winds and clouds a mercy, including winds that pollinate clouds and spread mercy, or send barren winds as punishment.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وتصريف الرياح والسحاب المسخر بين السماء والأرض ، قادر الله ربنا على ذلك اذا شاء

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b distinguishes Qur'anic plural “winds,” which denote mercy, from singular “wind,” which denotes punishment.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال : كل شئ في القران من الرياح فهي رحمة ، وكل شئ في القران

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b says clouds act as a sieve for rain, preventing falling water from damaging what it lands on; Ibn Abbas confirms he heard Ka'b say this.
rows.anchor: سمعته يقول : ان السحاب غربال المطر ، لولا السحاب حين ينزل الماء من السماء

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Ka'b also says that seed descends from the sky, explaining why different plants grow in different years; Ibn Abbas says he heard him say it.
rows.anchor: سمعته يقول : ان البذر ينزل من السماء . قال ابن عباس : سمعت ذلك من كعب

rows.speaker: أبو الضحى
rows.claim: Abu al-Duha explains that the signs from the creation of the heavens through this verse are signs for people who reason.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الضحى قال : انزل الله : ان في خلق السموات والأرض إلى قوله : لايات لقوم يعقلون

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Mu'adh reports that fasting initially prohibited food, drink, and sex only after a person slept; after Umar had intercourse with his wife after sleeping and told the Prophet, the verse permitting night intercourse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى عن معاذ بن جبل قال : احيل الصيام على ثلاثة احوال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses rafath as sexual intercourse; the source lists Ata, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, al-Hasan, al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and others in agreement.
rows.anchor: عن أبي اسحاق عن سعيد ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال : الرفث : الجماع .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says spouses are a source of tranquility for one another; Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada, al-Suddi, and Muqatil are reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن طاووس عن ابن عباس هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن قال : هن سكن لكم

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas interprets the spouses' clothing metaphor as each being a covering or blanket for the other.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن قال : هن لحاف لكم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik recounts that people once had to abstain from food and drink after sleeping during a fast; Umar and Ka'b each had intercourse after their wives had slept, then Umar informed the Prophet and this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه انه قال : كان الناس اذا صام الرجل فنام حرم عليه الطعام والشراب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains “you were betraying yourselves” as “you were wronging yourselves.”
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله تختانون انفسكم قال : تظلمون انفسكم .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the phrase as secretly having intercourse with their wives in violation of the former rule.
rows.anchor: عن السدى علم الله انكم كنتم تختانون انفسكم انكم تقعون عليهن خيانة .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas connects God's pardon to what Umar had done, saying God revealed His forgiveness in these words.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس علم الله انكم كنتم تختانون انفسكم يعني بذلك الذي فعل عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says “be intimate with them” means intercourse, expressed by God euphemistically; Mujahid, Ata, al-Dahhak, Muqatil, al-Suddi, and others agree.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس قال : المباشرة هو الجماع ولكن الله يكنى .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One interpretation of “seek what God has written for you” is to seek offspring; many early authorities are reported to share this view.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم قال : الولد .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second view from Ibn Abbas interprets what God has written as Laylat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الجوزاء عن ابن عباس وابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم قال : ليلة القدر .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the white and black threads as day and night: intimacy, eating, and drinking were permitted until dawn became clear, after which they were forbidden.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الابيض من الخيط الاسود يعني الليل والنهار

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the command to eat and drink was revealed concerning Abu Qays ibn Sirma of the Khazraj.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج وكلوا واشربوا قال : نزلت في أبي قيس بن صرمة من بني الخزرج .

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Adi ibn Hatim misunderstood the threads literally and watched two threads; the Prophet clarified that dawn means the whiteness of day and blackness of night.
rows.anchor: فاتيت النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم فاخبرته فضحك وقال : يا ابن حاتم الم اقل لك من الفجر

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl says the words “of dawn” were added after men tied white and black threads to their legs and ate until they could distinguish them; the clarification means night and day.
rows.anchor: عن سهل بن سعد قال : نزلت هذه الاية وكلوا واشربوا حتى يتبين لكم الخيط الابيض

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report from Ata describes dawn as the white dawn, with the transmitted wording apparently incomplete after “the one beneath it.”
rows.anchor: عن جابر عن عامر عن عطاء وقال : ذاكرتهما الفجر

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet forbade uninterrupted fasting for two days, likened it to Christian practice, and instructed Muslims to complete the fast until night and then break it.
rows.anchor: عن ليلى امراة بشير بن الخصاصية قالت : اردت ان اصوم يومين مواصلة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says the fast is over when night comes, day departs, and the sun has set.
rows.anchor: عن عمر قال : قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم : اذا اقبل الليل واخبر النهار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says intercourse is forbidden to anyone in retreat in a mosque, by night or day, until the retreat ends; Ibn Mas'ud, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Ata, Qatada, Mujahid, and others agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله ولا تباشروهن وأنتم عاكفون

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: When asked whether men who sleep in the mosque and become ritually impure should be reported to the ruler, Ibn Umar says they are the people in retreat.
rows.anchor: ابن عمر سئل عنهم فقال : هم العاكفون .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets God's boundaries as obedience to God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس تلك حدود الله يعني : طاعة الله .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi's second interpretation takes God's boundaries as His stipulations or conditions.
rows.anchor: عن السدى اما حدود الله : فشروطه .

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets God's boundaries as disobedience, specifically intercourse during retreat; Muqatil is reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك تلك حدود اللهقال : معصية الله ، يعني : المباشرة في الاعتكاف

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses “do not approach them” as “do not have intercourse.”
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان فلا تقربوها يعني : الجماع .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains “thus” as “in this way God makes His signs clear.”
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله عز وجل كذلك يعني : هكذا يبين الله اياته .

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil says God clarifies His signs so people will avoid sins.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله كذلك يبين الله اياته للناس لعلهم يتقون المعاصي

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil says every person in retreat must fast for as long as the retreat lasts.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله كذلك يبين الله اياته للناس لعلهم يتقون المعاصي وعلى كل معتكف الصيام ما دام معتكفا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses “so that they may be mindful” as “they obey.”
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد لعلهم يتقون قال يطيعون

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali identifies the passerby as the prophet Ezra, who left his city while young and came upon a ruined town; al-Hasan, al-Suddi, Ibn Burayda, and Qatada also identify him as Ezra.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب يعني قوله : أو كالذي مر على قرية قال : خرج عزير نبي الله من مدينته

rows.speaker: رجل من أهل الشام
rows.claim: A Syrian man gives a different identification: the person whom God caused to die for a hundred years was Hizqil ibn Buzā.
rows.anchor: سمعت رجلا من اهل الشام يقول : ان الذي اماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه ، اسمه : حزقيل بن بوزا .

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: Ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr says the man was a prophet named Irmiya; Mujahid instead identifies him as an Israelite, and Wahb is reported to agree with Mujahid.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عبيد ابن عمير : انه كان نبيا ، وكان اسمه : ارميا وقال مجاهد : رجل من بني اسرائيل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the man was Ezra visiting Jerusalem after Nebuchadnezzar the Babylonian destroyed it; al-Dahhak is reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ، في قول الله : أو كالذي مر على قرية قال : كنا نحدث انه عزير

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says “empty” means ruined.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله : وهي خاوية قال : خواها : خرابها .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains that the ruined town had no one in it.
rows.anchor: عن قتاده ، قوله : وهي خاوية قال : ليس فيها أحد .

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets its collapsed roofs as the roofs themselves; al-Suddi agrees.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله : على عروشها سقوفها .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada paraphrases the passerby's question as asking how God will rebuild the town after its ruin; al-Rabi ibn Anas gives the same interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة يعني في قوله الله : اني يحيى هذه الله بعد موتها قال : اني يعمر هذه بعد خرابها ؟

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi pictures Ezra arriving from Syria with a donkey, grapes, juice, and figs; on seeing the ruined town he gestured and asked how God would revive it, without denying or doubting resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن السدى ان عزيرا جاء من الشام على حمار له ، معه عنب وعصير وتين

rows.speaker: اسباط
rows.claim: The report says God caused the man and his donkey to die, and a hundred years passed over them.
rows.anchor: ثنا اسباط ، في قوله : فاماته الله مائة عام قال : فاماته اللله وامات حماره وهلكا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God punished an Israelite for asking the question: the donkey stood beside him without food or drink for a hundred years while his food and drink remained nearby.
rows.anchor: سالت الحسن ، عن قوله : اني يحيى هذه الله بعد موتها قال : هذا رجل من بني اسرائيل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the man died at the beginning of the day and was raised after a hundred years.
rows.anchor: عن قتاده ، في قوله : اني يحيى هذه الله بعد موتها فاماته الله اول النهار

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb identifies the man as Jeremiah, who asked the question after Jerusalem and its books were destroyed; God restored his spirit after a century, when the city had been rebuilt, following an initial return of Israelites after seventy years and thirty years of rebuilding.
rows.anchor: سمع وهب بن منبه في قوله : اني يحيى هذه الله بعد موتها يقول : ان ارميا ، لما خرب بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali says that when Ezra was raised after a hundred years, his eyes were the first part of him created.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب : اني يحيى هذه الله بعد موتها فاماته الله مائة عام ثم بعثه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says God then brought Ezra back to life.
rows.anchor: عن السدى في قوله : ثم بعثه ثم ان الله احيا عزيرا .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Ezra was raised at the end of the day; al-Rabi says he was raised before sunset.
rows.anchor: عن قتاده ، في قوله : ثم بعثه في اخر النهار .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the man thought he had stayed a day, then saw the remaining sun and revised this to part of a day; al-Hasan and al-Rabi give a similar account.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله : قال كم لبثت قال لبثت يوما ثم التفت ، فراى بقية الشمس

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali's account says Ezra's bones came together, were clothed with flesh, and received a spirit; returning to his city as a young man, he found his young shoemaker neighbor now old.
rows.anchor: عن ناجية بن كعب الاسدى ، عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : خرج عزير نبي الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says Ezra's food was a basket of figs; Wahb ibn Munabbih and Mujahid are reported to give the same account.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ، قال : كان طعامه الذي معه ، سلة من تين .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the food as figs and grapes.
rows.anchor: عن السدى فانظر إلى طعامك من التين والعنب

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb identifies the drink as water kept in a small vessel.
rows.anchor: سمع وهب بن منبه في قوله : فانظر إلى طعامك وشرابك قال : قلة فيها ماء .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the drink as a skin filled with grape juice.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد عن قتادة : وشرابه : زق من عصير .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the food as a basket of figs and the drink as a skin of wine or juice.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد فانظر إلى طعامك قال : سلة تين وشرابك قال : زق خمر .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says “it did not change” means the food and drink remained unchanged; al-Hasan, Mujahid, Wahb, Qatada, and others agree.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : لم يتسنه لم يتغير .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak's report from Ibn Abbas stresses that food and drink remained unspoiled for a full hundred years, an extraordinary sign because they normally spoil sooner.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : فانظر إلى طعامك وشرابك لم يتسنه يقول : لم يتغير

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the figs did not turn sour and the juice did not ferment over the hundred years; both remained lawful and unchanged.
rows.anchor: عن السدى لم يتسنه يقول لم يتغير ، فيحمض التين والعنب ، ولم يختمر العصير

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's second gloss of “لم يتسنه” is “it did not putrefy.”
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد لم يتسنه : لم ينتن .

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala reads the word as “لم يتسن” and explains that the years had not passed over it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء لم يتسن لم تات عليه السنون

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the donkey's separated joints came together one by one and were then clothed with flesh.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة وانظر إلى حمارك قال : لما قدم نظر إلى مفاصله متفرقة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the donkey had died and its bones had decayed.
rows.anchor: عن السدى وانظر إلى حمادك وقد هلكت وبليت عظامه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says Ezra watched God bring the donkey back to life.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد يعني قوله : وانظر إلى حمارك قال : فنظر إلى حماره ، حين يحييه الله

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas says the donkey remained beside Ezra just as it was.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس وانظر إلى حمارك وكان حماره عنده كما هو

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the man was raised young after 140 years, while his sons had become centenarian elders; al-A'mash and al-Minhal ibn Amr are reported to give the same contrast.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : ولنجعلك آية للناس قال كان بعث ابن لمائة واربعين ، شابا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God made the man a sign by showing him this lesson in his own person.
rows.anchor: سالت الحسن ، عن قوله : ولنجعلك آية للناس قال : فكان هذا عبدا نفعه الله بما اراه من العبرة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Ezra returned to find his home rebuilt and his acquaintances dead; after proving his identity, his relatives vacated the house and returned it to him.
rows.anchor: عن السدى ، يعني قوله : ولنجعلك آية للناس قال : فرجع إلى اهله ، فوجد داره قد يبعث

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas glosses “a sign” as “a lesson.”
rows.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس ، قوله : آية يقول : عبرة .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “how We raise them” as making the bones stand up or rise, limb by limb.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها نشخصها عضوا عضوا .

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb says Ezra watched as the bones joined one another.
rows.anchor: سمع وهب بن منبه ، يعني في قوله : كيف ننشزها قال : فجعل ينظر إلى العظام

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the bones being raised as being moved and then clothed; a wind gathered the donkey's bones from hills and plains, where animals had scattered them, and assembled a fleshless skeleton before Ezra.
rows.anchor: عن السدى قوله : وانظر إلى العظام كيف ننشزها يقول : نحركها ثم نكسوها

rows.speaker: أبو حفص مبشر بن عبيد
rows.claim: Abu Hafs Mubashshir ibn Ubayd reports a reading, “كيف ننشزها,” with the meaning “we raise them upright.”
rows.anchor: عن أبي حفص مبشر بن عبيد ، في قراءته كيف ننشزها قال : نقيمها .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says God clothed the bones with flesh and blood, then an angel blew into the donkey's nostril and it brayed.
rows.anchor: عن السدى ثم نكسوها لحما قال : ان الله كسا العظام لحما ودما ، فقام حمارا

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima describes the joined joints being clothed in flesh, then nerves and skin, before breath was blown into the donkey's nostril and it brayed.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة يعني قوله : ثم نكسوها لحما قال : لما اتصلت المفاصل ، كسبت لحما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the eyes were created first, and Ezra watched the rest of his body form and the bones receive flesh so he would learn that God revives the dead and can do all things.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن ، قال ذكر لنا - والله اعلم - ن اول شيء خلقه الله منه ، عيناه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the statement “when it became clear to him, he said, ‘I know that God is powerful over everything’” was said to the man.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : فلما تبين له قال اعلم ان الله على كل شيء قدير قال : انما قيل له ذلك .

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq explains that God can do whatever He wills with His servants, whether punishment or forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق ان الله على كل شيء قدير اي : ان الله على كل ما اراد بعباده ، من نقمة

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makhul interprets spending in God's path as tethered horses prepared for service in God's cause.
rows.anchor: عن مكحول في قوله : الذين ينفقون اموالهم في سبيل الله قال هي الخيل الربيط في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses “in God's path” as “in obedience to God.”
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : في سبيل الله يعني : في طاعة الله .

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar says that after hearing of the seven-hundredfold reward, the Prophet asked for more for his community; God then revealed 2:245, and after another request, 39:10.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : لما نزلت مثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima calculates the parable's yield as seven hundred grains per seed.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة ، في قوله : مثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة انبتت

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says this seven-hundredfold reward is for whoever spends in God's path.
rows.anchor: عن السدى كمثل حبة انبتت سبع سنابل في كل سنبلة مائة حبة فهذا لمن انفق

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi says those in Medina who pledged to the Prophet and only went on expeditions with his permission received seven hundredfold for a good deed, while pledging to Islam brought tenfold.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع قوله : مثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة انبتت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says pilgrimage spending and jihad spending are equal: each dirham receives seven hundredfold because both are in God's path.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قول الله تعالى : مثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم في سبيل الله كمثل حبة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that God multiplies a good deed two thousandfold.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، يقول ان الله عز وجل يضاعف الحسنة الفي الف حسنة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says a person who funds an expedition while staying home receives seven hundredfold for each dirham, while one who goes and spends on the campaign receives seven hundred thousandfold; he recites this verse.
rows.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : من ارسل نفقة في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains “knowing” as knowing what will happen.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : عليم يعني بما يكون .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan describes people who send someone on an expedition or support a recipient, then remind and hurt them by boasting of their spending; such reminders are not counted as sincerely seeking God's reward.
rows.anchor: قال : سألت الحسن ، عن قوله : الذين ينفقون اموالهم في سبيل الله ثم لا يتبعون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God knew some people would remind others of their gifts and disliked that behavior.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : ثم لا يتبعون ما انفقوا منا ولا اذى قال : قد علم الله ان اناسا سيمنون عطاءهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report reaching Amr ibn Dinar says the Prophet declared that no charity is dearer to God than a kind word, citing this verse.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن دينار ، قال : بلغنا ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ما من صدقة احب إلى الله من صدقة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God knew some people would remind others of gifts, disliked it, and therefore commended kind speech and forgiveness over charity followed by harm.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ، قال : علم الله ان ناسا يمنون عطيتهم ، فكره ذلك ، وقدم فيه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains “God is self-sufficient” as meaning that God has no need of your charities.
rows.anchor: عن البراء والله غني عن صاقاتكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God informed His servants of His forbearance, compassion, generosity, vast mercy, and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس اخبر الله عباده بحلمه وعطفه وكرمه وسعة رحمته ومغفرته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas recounts a warning that habitual wine drinkers, those who disobey parents, and boastful donors will not enter Paradise; he found this verse addressing the donor and was relieved that sinners could still repent.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : لا يدخل الجنة مدمن خمر ولا عاق ، ولا منان

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says donations are invalidated by reminders and harm just as an ostentatious donation is invalidated.
rows.anchor: عن السدى قوله : لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والاذى فتبطل كما بطلت صدقة الرياء .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God disliked this behavior for believers.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم قال . كره الله ذلك للمؤمنين

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil explains “reminding” as the donor reminding the recipient of the donation.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قول الله تعالى : لا تبطلوا صدقاتكم بالمن والاذى هو الرجل يمن صدقته

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil explains “harm” as hurting the person who receives the charity.
rows.anchor: وبه عن مقاتل بن حيان في قول الله : بالمن والاذى قال : يؤذى الذي يتصدق عليه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi compares ostentatious spending to rain washing soil off a smooth stone: the money is lost to showing off and yields no reward.
rows.anchor: عن السدى ، قوله : كالذي ينفق ماله رئاء الناس ، فكذلك هذا الذي ينفق ماله رياء الناس

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets the one who does not believe in God and the Last Day as a hypocrite.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قول الله : ولا يؤمن بالله واليوم الاخر يعني : المنافق .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains not believing in God as failing to affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : ولا يؤمن بالله يعني : لا يصدقون بتوحيد الله .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the smooth-stone parable represents the deeds of unbelievers on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : فمثله كمثل صفوان عليه تراب قال : هذا مثل ضربه الله تعالى ، لاعمال الكفار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses “safwan” as a smooth rock; Ikrima, al-Hasan, al-Suddi, al-Rabi, Qatada, and Muqatil are reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : صفوان يعني : الحجر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima explains “wabil” as rain that takes away the soil; al-Rabi and Qatada specify that it is heavy rain.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة ، في قوله : فاصابه وابل والوابل : المطر فذهب بما عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “left bare” as left dry, fruitless, and disgraced.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : فتركه صلدا يقول : فتركه يابسا خاسئا لا ينبت شيئا

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil says those who spend ostentatiously cannot benefit from what they earned: they receive no reward and it will not help them on Judgment Day; the text also notes his explanations came from Successors including al-Dahhak and Jabir ibn Zayd.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان في قوله الله لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا يعني به : نفقاتهم

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi says that on that Day the ostentatious donors can do nothing with their deeds, just as rain leaves the stone clean; Qatada agrees.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع ، في قوله : لا يقدرون على شيء مما كسبوا يومئذ ، كما ترك المطر الصفا نقيا

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses spending to seek God's pleasure as spending in expectation of reward from Him.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، قوله ومثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله قال : احتسابا .

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi says this is a parable God gives for the work of a believer.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس ، قوله : ومثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله قال : هذا مثل ضربه الله لعمل المؤمن

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says such spenders seek God's pleasure and do not seek reputation or to be seen by people.
rows.anchor: سالت الحسن ، عن قوله : ومثل الذين ينفقون اموالهم ابتغاء مرضات الله قال : ينفقون ابتغاء مرضات الله

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi interprets “as confirmation from themselves” as inward certainty; another report says it means certainty and affirmation, and al-Suddi and Muqatil are reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي وتثبيتا من انفسهم قال : يقينا من انفسهم .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid's second interpretation is that the spenders make sure where they place their money.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد وتثبيتا من انفسهم قال : يثبتون اين يضعون اموالهم .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Salih, and Maymun ibn Mihran interpret the phrase as choosing the proper recipients or places for zakat.
rows.anchor: وروى عن الحسن وابا صالح ، وميمون بن مهران ، قالوا : مواضع الزكاة .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the phrase as spending while expecting reward from God.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : وتثبيتا من انفسهم قال : احتسابا من انفسهم .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says a rabwa is an elevated, level place.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد 1 قوله : كمثل جنة بربوة قال : الربوه : المكان الظاهر المستوي .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr defines a rabwa as a raised part of the ground; al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Rabi, Ata, and Muqatil are reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، قال : الربوة : النشز من الأرض .

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil says the wabil is rain.
rows.anchor: مقاتل بن حيانفاصابها وابل يقول : اصاب الجنه المطر .

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Ata al-Khurasani calls wabil abundant or copious rain.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني قال : الوابل : الجود من المطر .

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil says “its produce twice over” means the garden bears twice the fruit.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حين قوله : فئاتت اكلها يعني : ثمرتها ضعفين .

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi applies the doubled harvest to the spender, whose reward is multiplied twofold.
rows.anchor: عن السدى فئاتت اكلها ضعفين كلما اضعفت ثمر تلك الجنة

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam says this describes Egyptian land: dew makes it productive, and heavy rain doubles its yield.
rows.anchor: سمعت زيد بن اسلم يقول في قول الله : فان لم يصبها وابل فطل قال : تلك ارض مصر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses tal as dew; several authorities agree, though al-Rabi calls it a light shower.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ، في قول الله : فان لم يصبها وابل فطل قال : الطل : الندى .

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil glosses tal as a fine drizzle of rain.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل : فطل يعني بالطل : الرذاذ من المطر .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden parable describes a person who spends without seeking reputation or display and does not remind recipients of the gift.
rows.anchor: فهذا مثل من لا ينفق ماله رياء وسمعة ، ولا يمن به على من يعطيه .

rows.speaker: جويبر
rows.claim: Juwair calls tal “al-rakk,” then explains that term as gentle rain.
rows.anchor: قال جويبر ، في قوله : فان لم يصبها وابل فطل قال : الرك من المطر .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says this parable teaches that God's promise for the believer's work will not fail, just as the garden's good yield does not fail whether it receives heavy rain or drizzle.
rows.anchor: عن قنادة ، قوله : والله بما تعملون بصير هذا مثل ضربه الله لعمل المؤمن ، يقول : ليس لخبره خلف

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabi interprets the question as asking whether anyone would want to live in error and sin, die, and then find his deeds lost when he most needs them, as God asks what good he sent ahead.
rows.anchor: عن الربيع ، في قوله : ايود احدكم يقول : ايحب احدكم ان يعيش في الضلالة والمعاصي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the garden represents worldly life without obedience; after death, its owner is like an old man whose garden burns while his small children cannot help, just as the negligent person finds everything a regret.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قوله : ايود احدكم ان تكون له جنة قال : دنيا لا يعمل فيها بطاعة الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the fruitful garden as what a person has fashioned or achieved in youth.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : ايود احدكم ان تكون له جنة من نخيل واعناب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a discussion led by Umar, Ibn Abbas says the parable depicts a wealthy worshipper whose works are drowned after Satan leads him into sins; Umar accepts the interpretation as a parable for deeds.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، وسمعت أبا بكر ابن أبي مليكة يحدث عن عبيد بن عمير ، قال : قال عمر يوما لاصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the garden represents a person who worked in faith, good deeds, charity, and spending but committed shirk or a major sin at the end of life, voiding his deeds and dying an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني ، عن عكرمة ايود احدكم ان تكون له جنة من نخيل واعناب قال : هذا مثل لرجل يعمل بالايمان

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi calls this another parable for ostentatious spending: the donor's money earns no reward and, when needed at the Resurrection, proves burned away like the garden.
rows.anchor: عن السدى ايود احدكم ان تكون له جنة من نخيل واعناب تجري من تحتها الانهار

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says every kind of tree in this world exists in Paradise, even colocynth.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة ، قوله : فيها من كل الثمرات فما في الدنيا من شجرة الا وهي في الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the mention of weak offspring is part of the parable.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وله ذرية ضعفاء قال مثل ضرب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas expands the parable: a person's youthful work is lost in old age when a fiery whirlwind destroys his garden and weak children cannot help; likewise the unbeliever arrives before God with no good, while the believer's stored reward awaits him. He contrasts the believer's stored eternal honor with the wealthy unbeliever's lasting punishment for boasting and doubting the meeting with God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : ضرب الله مثلا حسنا وكل امثاله حسن ، قال : ايود احدكم ان تكون له جنة من نخيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the whirlwind as a wind; al-Suddi and al-Rabi are reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : اعصار قال : ريح .

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan gives a second gloss for the whirlwind: a cold blast or frost.
rows.anchor: كان الحسن يقول فاصابها اعصار يقول : صر ، برد .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the fire in the whirlwind is an intensely scorching wind; al-Suddi, Mujahid, and al-Rabi are reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : فيه نار قال : ريح فيها سموم شديدة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the garden is lost precisely when its owner most needs it, illustrating deeds lost when they are most needed.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن ، قوله : فاحترقت قال : فذهبت احوج ما كان اليها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the garden itself burned.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه ، عن جده عن ابن عباس قوله : فاحترقت قال : فاحترق بستانه .

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains “thus God makes the signs clear” as referring to what has just been mentioned.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : كذلك يبين الله لكم الايات يعني ما ذكر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses “so that you may reflect” as “so that you may obey.”
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : لعلكم تتفكرون : لعلكم تطيعون .

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says this is a parable to be understood and pondered; only the learned grasp such parables, quoting 29:43.
rows.anchor: هذا مثل ضربه الله فاعقلوا عن الله امثاله ، يقول

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri says that when God addresses “O you who believe,” the Prophet is included among the believers.
rows.anchor: عن الاوزاعي عن الزهري ، قال : اذا قال الله : يايها الذين امنوا فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، منهم .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “spend” as “give charity”; Muqatil is reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : انفقوا يقول : تصدقوا .

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says “the good things you have earned” means your best and most wholesome possessions; al-Zuhri is reported to agree.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : انفقوا من طيبات ماكسبتم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Companions used to buy cheap food to give in charity, so God revealed this command to give from good earnings.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : كان اصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يشترون الطعام الرخيص ويتصدقون

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid first interprets produce from the earth as dates from palm trees, some of which people had been giving as inferior dates; they were told to give good produce instead.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله : ومما اخرجنا لكم من الأرض قال : النخل .

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid has a second reported interpretation of produce from the earth as plants, differing from his first interpretation as palm trees.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد ومما اخرجنا لكم من الأرض قال : النبت .

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil interprets produce from the earth as fruits, dates, raisins, grapes, and grain.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، قوله : ومما اخرجنا لكم من الأرض يعني به : الثمار ، التمر والزبيب

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib glosses “do not deliberately seek” as “do not intend.”
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب ، في قوله : ولا تيمموا يقول : لا تعمدوا

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Bara says the bad produce people should not deliberately give is inferior dried dates.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب في قوله : ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون يقول : لا تعمدوا للحشف

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن معقل
rows.claim: Ibn Ma'qil says a Muslim's earnings are not intrinsically bad, but one should not give inferior dates, counterfeit coins, or worthless property.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب عن عبد الله بن معقل ، في هذه الاية ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون

rows.speaker: عبيدة
rows.claim: Ubayda says the verse concerns obligatory zakat; for voluntary charity, even a date is acceptable, and a counterfeit coin is better than a date. A conflicting report from him is noted without its content.
rows.anchor: عن هشام ، عن ابن سيرين قال : قلت لعبيدة ولا تيمموا الخبيث منه تنفقون قال : هذا في الزكاة المفروضة
